key: IN the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, born Only Lord of all created beings. He fixed and holdeth up this earth and heaven. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
s: The verse opens a hymn whose verses, all but the last, end on one question; Sāyaṇa, on 10.121.1, takes ‘What’ as pointing to Prajapati, whose nature is not known, or as his name Ka, since he desires to create, or since he is happiness.

evidence.words: “कस्मै । अत्र किंशब्दोऽनिर्ज्ञातस्वरूपत्वात् प्रजापतौ वर्तते । यद्वा । सृष्ट्यर्थं कामयत इति कः । कमेर्डप्रत्ययः । यद्वा । कं सुखम् । तद्रूपत्वात् क इत्युच्यते ।
evidence.gloss: Kasmai: here the word kim (what, who) stands for Prajāpati, because his own nature is not ascertained. Or: he desires (kāmayate) for the sake of creation, hence Ka; the suffix ḍa after kam. Or: kam is happiness; because he has that form he is called Ka.
